newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - American Brands to spin off Gallaher tobacco.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - American Brands to spin off Gallaher tobacco.

text.p: American Brands Inc. said Tuesday that it was completing its exit from the tobacco business as the legal and regulatory climate for cigarette companies becomes tougher in the United States.

Shares of American Brands shot up 10 percent after the company, which also sells liquor, sports equipment and household hardware products, said it will spin off its British-based Gallaher tobacco business and then change its own name to Fortune Brands.
American Brands stock rose $4.625, or 10 percent, to $49.125 on the New York Stock Exchange in early trading but then slipped back to trade at $48, up $3.50, late in the day.

The company, whose products include Jim Beam bourbon, Master Lock padlocks and Titleist, Foot-Joy and Cobra golf equipment, said that as part of the divestiture Gallaher will pay Fortune Brands about $1.4 billion.
After the deal goes through, the company said, the new Fortune Brands will use the after-tax proceeds of about $1.25 billion to pay down short-term debt and finance further growth.
Chairman Thomas Hays said the company would be well positioned to continue its aggressive acquisition program, which scored a stunning success with its purchase last year of Cobra Golf.
"We intend to support all of our companies," Hays said in discussing possible areas of expansion.

American Brands, which sold off its U.S. tobacco operations in 1994, said the Gallaher spinoff would strengthen the British-based company by removing it from the current harsh environment for cigarette makers in the United States.
The business environment for tobacco sales in the United States has never been more threatening, with lawsuits mounting and a new level of regulatory oversight being undertaken by federal authorties.

With sales of over $6.5 billion for the 12 months through June, Gallaher, whose major brands include Benson and Hedges and Silk Cut, is the tobacco market leader in Britain, with strong international sales, principally in Europe.
American Brands denied that its spinoff plan was in response to a recent announcement that 40 British smokers plan to sue Gallaher in London.
"The company spent many months thoroughly reviewing various alternatives, so it has nothing to do with anything that happened 10 days ago," a spokesman said.

While American Brands effectively removed itself from the potential liabilities of the tobacco industry when it sold its U.S. tobacco operations in 1994, Hays acknowledged that the divestiture would reinforce the perception that the company had isolated itself from possible litigation.
"I think it's part of the benefit, certainly," Hays said in an interview. "There was some ongoing confusion: Were we still in the domestic tobacco business."
"I don't think there's any qustion but that the presence of the tobacco business hurt the valuation (of American Brands stock)," said UBS Securities analyst Anton Brenner. "This will remove that."

American Brands, which will retain its headquarters in Old Greenwich, Conn., said the move will allow it to concentrate on its other business lines, which produced $4.6 billion in sales in the 12 months through June.

The company said that when it becomes Fortune Brands, it expects earnings growth of between 13 percent and 15 percent a year. "That's substantially higher than the 10 percent goal we had established for American Brands," the company said.
Eleven of its brands had sales of more than $100 million last year, including Jim Beam and DeKuyper liquors, Titleist, Foot-Joy and Cobra golf equipment and Master Lock padlocks.

The company said that after the split-up, Fortune's dividend would be about 80 cents a year and Gallaher's would be about $1.20, or 77 pence, although future dividends will be determined by the boards of the respective companies.
American Brands said it expected shares of Gallaher to be listed on the London Stock Exchange and on the New York Stock Exchange in the form of American Depositary Receipts.
It added that Gallaher planned to borrow about $1.4 billion to pay for the transaction.
American Brands said that once the spinoff was completed, the new Fortune Brands will consider repurchasing up to 10 million Fortune shares.
The company said the spinoff was contingent upon favorable tax rulings, which are more complex due to the international aspects of the transaction.
